cause_quote: The original web renderer set `const label = subagentActivityLabel(task);` and rendered that status-derived string as the row label, so it never used the supplied task title to identify the row.
user_saw: Concurrent child tasks had the same generic heading in web and macOS chat, making them hard to tell apart.
summary: Web and macOS chat now lead with the Gateway-supplied task title, show status and progress separately, and fall back to a generic heading when the title is blank or missing.
reasoning: I checked both introducing diffs. The first web implementation used generic headings even for named tasks, and the separate native implementation in #121815 likewise rendered a status-derived title. The later web change in #146667 added task names to the preview while retaining the generic heading.
